# Pending Orders from the Till

When a sale is started at the till, the order is created in OrderHub straight away — before the money is taken. Until payment goes through, it sits as **Pending** and shows **Payment not completed**.

This is deliberate. It means nothing is sent to production and no job tickets print for a sale that was never paid for. The trade-off is that if a customer changes their mind at the card machine, or a payment fails and they walk out, the order stays in your list waiting for someone to deal with it.

![Pending Order in OrderHub](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/1a4d55e8-d61a-41eb-9648-14b44be3e46e.png)

---

## What a pending till order has and hasn't done

| | |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Created in OrderHub** | Yes — you'll see it in **Orders** right away |
| **Stock taken** | **Yes** — the items are reserved for this order |
| **Job tickets printed** | No |
| **In production queues or Pickup** | No |
| **Customer notified** | No |

The important one is stock. A pending order holds its items, so your on-hand figures already count them as gone.

---

## Telling them apart from web orders

**Pending** is also the normal starting status for orders arriving from your website. Those are a different thing and need no action.

A pending order from the till is the one labelled **Payment not completed**. If it doesn't carry that label, it's a normal web order going through its usual route.

---

## Dealing with one

There are three tidy endings. Pick whichever matches what actually happened.

### The customer paid

Open the order and use **Collect Payment** to record the money — cash, a card machine, or any other method. Recording the payment confirms the order and generates its job tickets. See **Order Payment**.

### The customer is going ahead, but isn't paying yet

Use this when the sale is happening but the money comes later — paying on account, or on collection.

1. Open **Orders** and find the order.
2. Click **Update** on the order row.
3. Set the status to **Confirmed**.
4. Tick the notification option if you want the customer told.

![Change Order status to Confirmed](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/1e5e1b94-22d7-49ba-9138-64356eee168c.png)

* Note: If every item on the sale was something handed straight over the counter, you'll see **Confirmed. All items were handed over at the till — mark the order Completed when the customer has it.** Nothing goes to production in that case, so mark the order **Completed** once the customer has their items.
* Note: If you see **Order confirmed, but we couldn't confirm its job tickets were generated**, the order is still confirmed. Open it and use **Regenerate tickets** if they're missing.

### The sale isn't happening

Use this when the customer left, the payment failed and wasn't retried, or the order was started by mistake.

**Cancel the order** from **Orders**. Cancelling releases the stock back to your shelf count. This is the step that keeps your inventory honest — a pending order left sitting there holds its stock indefinitely.

![Cancelling a pending order](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/3ca1f970-13e8-4a76-bd40-bdf7ff28e9cf.png)

---

## Good to know

* **You'll be alerted.** Pending till orders appear in your alerts, so you don't have to go looking for them.
* **Nothing clears these up by itself.** Pending till orders stay until someone confirms or cancels them, and they don't appear in production queues or the **Pickup** list. Make checking them part of the end-of-day routine.
* **Adding items after tapping Charge.** Tapping **Charge** creates the order. If you close the payment window to add another item and charge again, the first order is left behind as pending with its stock held. Cancel it from **Orders**.
* **Cancelling is safe.** It releases the stock and leaves a record of what happened.
